days.title: 1,190 finds
days.pitch: Every geocache I've found as Hipparchus, one dot each, coloured by year. Twenty-odd years of where curiosity has taken me.
days.alt: Map of 1,190 geocaches found by Hipparchus from 2001 to 2026, as small dots coloured from pale gold for early years to dark red for recent ones. The main map covers the West Coast, where most are, thickest in Washington, California, Nevada. A small world map below shows finds in 25 countries, and a bar chart shows finds per year, with the most in 2017.

days.title: The Seawall
days.pitch: The path around Stanley Park in Vancouver: 8.75 km of Seawall between the forest and the sea, on a Mapbox Outdoors basemap, with the landmarks along the way.
days.alt: Map of Stanley Park in Vancouver with the Seawall drawn as a red line around its shore, about 8.8 km, and landmarks including Beaver Lake, Brockton Point Lighthouse, Lumberman's Arch, Nine O'Clock Gun, Prospect Point.

days.title: Every fire around Groveland
days.pitch: Every recorded fire perimeter in Tuolumne County since the early 1900s, oldest faint, newest bright, with the Rim Fire (2013) wrapped around Groveland.
days.alt: Map of Tuolumne County, California, covered in overlapping semi-transparent fire perimeters from 1900 to 2025, pale for old fires and red for recent ones. The 2013 Rim Fire, outlined with a dashed line, fills much of the middle of the county east of Groveland. 36% of the county has burned at least once and 16% twice or more.

days.title: Rainier's swarms
days.pitch: Earthquakes within 30 km of Mount Rainier since 2000, grouped into swarms by space and time. The July 2025 swarm, the largest ever recorded there, stands out.
data: USGS ComCat earthquake catalog (API, no key)

data_links.name: USGS ComCat earthquake catalog (API, no key)

days.alt: Shaded relief map of Mount Rainier with 11,408 earthquakes since 2000 as dots within a 30 km circle. Most are grey background quakes, with coloured clusters marking swarms; the largest, 1,362 quakes in July 2025, sits just under the summit. A bar chart of quakes per month shows a spike for each swarm.

days.title: Where you can see Rainier from
days.pitch: A viewshed from the summit of Mount Rainier over 30 m terrain, with Earth's curvature and refraction, showing every place in Washington with a line of sight to the mountain.
days.alt: Shaded relief map of Washington and northern Oregon with the areas that can see Mount Rainier's summit shaded red: 35,267 square kilometres of land, reaching 390 km to the northwest at the farthest. Cities with a line of sight: Seattle, Tacoma, Lakewood, Olympia, Everett, Victoria, Portland, Yakima, Ellensburg, Aberdeen. Cities without: Bellingham, Vancouver, Salem, Wenatchee, Tri-Cities, Port Angeles, Spokane.

days.title: Tasman to Cook
days.pitch: James Cook's 1772 chart of New Zealand, lined up with today's coast, with the stretches Abel Tasman saw in 1642–43 in gold. A map version of my Cartographic Perspectives article.
data: Cook's Chart of New-Zealand (1772), Royal Museums Greenwich F0293, via Wikimedia Commons
Tasman map (c. 1644), State Library of New South Wales, via Wikimedia Commons

data_links.name: Cook's Chart of New-Zealand (1772), Royal Museums Greenwich F0293, via Wikimedia Commons
Tasman map (c. 1644), State Library of New South Wales, via Wikimedia Commons

deeper.name: My review of A Draught of the South Land, Cartographic Perspectives

days.alt: James Cook's 1772 engraved chart of New Zealand, georeferenced, with today's coastline traced over it in red; the two match closely, except that Banks Peninsula is drawn as an island, Stewart Island as part of the mainland, and much of the coast sits slightly east. Gold lines mark the west coasts Abel Tasman saw in 1642-43, with an inset of Tasman's own coastline from the Bonaparte map of about 1644.

days.title: Ten minutes, on the clock
days.pitch: Whatever the day brings, made in ten minutes with a timer visible in the corner of the screenshot.

days.title: Paradise, Eden, Utopia
days.pitch: Every place in the United States named Paradise, Eden, Utopia, Arcadia or Shangri-La, from Paradise on Rainier to Utopia, Texas.
days.alt: Map of the lower 48 states dotted with 836 places named Paradise, Eden, Arcadia, Utopia or Shangri-La. Paradise (501) is the most common, then Eden (243). Only 264 are towns; the most common kinds are townships and other civil divisions, streams, valleys.

days.title: Tacoma to Paradise
days.pitch: One line from the Port of Tacoma to Paradise on Rainier, and what changes along it: people, buildings, trees and elevation.
days.alt: A map of the straight line from the Port of Tacoma to Paradise on Mount Rainier over a street and forest map and census population, with two profiles below: people per square kilometre, high in Tacoma and Puyallup and falling to almost none after about km 29, and elevation rising to 8,850 ft on Rainier's flank before Paradise.

days.title: A map made only by asking
days.pitch: Big Creek's watershed above Groveland as a 1960s line-printer map: a FORTRAN program, written entirely from a one-sentence prompt, prints the basin in eight overprinted tones on green-bar paper, the way SYMAP did. The prompts are posted with it.

data_links.name: USGS NLDI (basin and flowlines for gage 11284400)

deeper.name: PUGET-TIDES: tides of Puget Sound in FORTRAN
CASCADIA-WX: Northwest weather balloons in FORTRAN

days.alt: A green-bar line-printer printout of Big Creek's watershed near Groveland, California: the basin outlined in asterisks and shaded in eight tones of typed characters, darker where higher, with streams left as blank gaps, a G at the gage, and a typed legend of elevation classes, cells and percent of area below.

days.title: Follow a raindrop
days.pitch: Click anywhere in the Sierra and watch where the water goes, river by river, to the sea, using the USGS's navigation service.
days.alt: Screenshot of the Follow a raindrop page: a raindrop starting near Groveland traced down the Tuolumne and San Joaquin rivers to the Delta, 279 km, on a pale basemap.

days.title: Inside Kīlauea
days.pitch: The earthquakes beneath Kīlauea's summit in cross-section, sketching the magma plumbing that the surface hides.
days.alt: Left, a shaded-relief map of Kīlauea's summit dotted with 19,466 earthquake epicentres since 2019; right, a north-south cross-section through Halema‘uma‘u showing where the earthquakes cluster with depth.

days.pitch: Night lights across Nevada and Utah, with Great Basin National Park's dark sky set against the glow of Las Vegas and Salt Lake City.

DarkSky International: Great Basin National Park (Dark Sky Park, 2016)

data_links.name: NASA Black Marble, via NASA GIBS (no login)

days.title: Nobody lives here
days.pitch: Nevada's 2020 census blocks with a population of zero. Most of the state is null.
days.alt: Map of Nevada's census blocks: 77% of the land is pale, where nobody lived in 2020; light grey blocks hold a few people each; black specks around Las Vegas, Reno and the towns hold nine in ten Nevadans on 0.4% of the land.

days.title: Kangaroo rats in hexagons
days.pitch: Every Dipodomys observation across the Southwest and Great Basin, binned into H3 hexagons. A return to my 2023 Day 1.
days.alt: Hexagon map of western North America shaded by how many kangaroo rat records each holds, 96,883 in all across 1,694 hexagons; the busiest holds 3,143. Death Valley is marked.

days.title: Groveland, by volunteers
days.pitch: Everything OpenStreetMap knows about Groveland and Big Oak Flat, after I add what's missing.
days.alt: Map of Groveland and Big Oak Flat, California, drawn only from OpenStreetMap: 3,437 buildings in red, roads in black, paths dashed, streams in blue and 52 named places in gold along Highway 120.

days.title: The world from Lakewood
days.pitch: An azimuthal equidistant map centred on Lakewood, where straight lines from the centre are true distances, to everywhere I've been, from Namibia to Guadeloupe.
days.alt: A round world map centred on Lakewood, Washington, in an azimuthal equidistant projection, with red lines out to the 37 countries I've been to and a few places closer to home. Africa: 7 countries, 13,545 to 16,450 km; Caribbean: 11 countries, 4,798 to 6,593 km; Europe: 14 countries, 5,905 to 9,819 km. Canada (330 km), Reno (877 km), Ruby Mountains (923 km), Groveland (1,054 km), Mexico (4,342 km), New Zealand (11,898 km), Australia (12,416 km), Indonesia (13,107 km). The farthest is South Africa.

days.title: Every brewery I've checked into
days.pitch: My Untappd check-ins, mapped by brewery, sized by how many beers.

deeper.name: HopLove: every hop in 2,000 Northwest beers

days.alt: Map of Cascadia with gold circles at 45 breweries, sized by how many different beers I've had from each in a year of Untappd check-ins; Kings & Daughters Brewery is biggest with 16. A list beside it names 22 breweries farther away.

days.title: Every stream that reaches Modesto
days.pitch: The whole Tuolumne river network above Modesto, by stream order, with the SIERRA-FLOW gages on it.
days.alt: Map of the Tuolumne River basin above Modesto, 4,742 square kilometres of the Sierra Nevada, with 3,825 kilometres of streams drawn thicker by stream order up to order 6, and the five SIERRA-FLOW gages marked.

days.title: A day of ground motion
days.pitch: A 24-hour helicorder from Camp Muir on Rainier, one line per hour. A map of time, or of a place?
days.alt: A helicorder: 24 horizontal wiggly lines, one per hour of July 8, 2025, recorded at Camp Muir on Mount Rainier, in alternating ink, red, blue and green. Gold dots mark the 352 earthquakes located nearby that day.

days.title: Lake Tahoe, clear and deep
days.pitch: Tahoe's floor, 497 m at the deepest, and beside it the lake's clarity on the same downward axis: how far a Secchi disk could be seen each year since 1968, from the record my SECCHI project keeps.
data: UC Davis TERC Secchi record (EDI, CC BY 4.0), via SECCHI

data_links.name: UC Davis TERC Secchi record (EDI, CC BY 4.0), via SECCHI

deeper.name: secchi: a modern Secchi disk for Lake Tahoe
Blog: A Plate on a Rope

days.alt: Map of Lake Tahoe's floor shaded blue by depth to 497 m, with 100 m contours, the deepest point and TERC's two Secchi stations marked. Beside it, bars hanging down from the surface show how far a Secchi disk could be seen each year since 1968: 31 m at best in 1968, 18 m at worst in 2021, and not at the 29.7 m target since 1970.

days.title: Every building in Washington
days.pitch: Every building in Washington from Overture Maps, queried with DuckDB's spatial extension and drawn with lonboard. Both new to me.
days.alt: Dark map of Washington State where each half-kilometre cell glows by how many of Overture Maps' 3,817,375 building footprints it holds, brightest around Puget Sound and Spokane. A panel shows who drew the footprints, led by OpenStreetMap volunteers at 72%.

days.title: Did you feel it? Nisqually, 2001
days.pitch: The M6.8 Nisqually earthquake of February 28, 2001, as the people who felt it reported it, from USGS "Did You Feel It?".
data: USGS ComCat event uw10530748, DYFI product

data_links.name: USGS ComCat event uw10530748, DYFI product

days.alt: Map of the Pacific Northwest showing how strongly people felt the magnitude 6.8 Nisqually earthquake of February 28, 2001. Small squares coloured from pale (weak) to dark red (very strong) cover western Washington, strongest around the epicenter at the south end of Puget Sound near Olympia, Lakewood and Tacoma, and fading toward Portland, Vancouver and Spokane. Based on 10,725 'Did You Feel It?' reports.

days.title: When Rainier's snow melted
days.pitch: Every 30 m patch of Mount Rainier coloured by the day it lost its snow in 2026, from Sentinel-2's scene classification, with the glaciers that never melted in white and Paradise's SNOTEL record from my snowpack tracker as ground truth.
data: Sentinel-2 L2A scene classification (Earth Search, AWS open data)
NRCS SNOTEL via STORM CHASER, my Rainier snowpack tracker

days.alt: Map of Mount Rainier with every 30 metre patch coloured by the date its snow melted in 2026, from tan in April in the valleys to deep blue in August high on the mountain, with the glaciers in white where the snow never melted. Below, Paradise SNOTEL's snow water equivalent through the 2026 water year against its median, with the satellite's melt-out date for Paradise marked.

days.title: If you hit the third cattle guard
days.pitch: The hot-spring napkin from my memoir, redrawn by hand in bar ink on a cocktail napkin: the springs outside Bridgeport and the roads between them, with directions counted in cattle guards, not miles. Drawn from memory, like the original.
